instruction:
Make Alpha from Mesh (z-height map)

Look at `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj`. It is a button-shaped SubTool named 'Button': a flat disk of radius 0.5 BU and thickness 0.1 BU with a slight central dome of height 0.04 BU (total peak z = 0.14 BU). The disk sits with its flat bottom at z=0 and circular axis along +Z.

Load this mesh into ZBrush, orient the view looking straight down the +Z axis at the button's top surface, and use Alpha > MakeAlphaFromMesh to bake a grayscale height map. Export it as a 512x512 single-channel PNG `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Button.png`, encoding the top-surface z-height per pixel (bright = tall, dark = no button).

Pass criteria:
- `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Button.png` exists, is parseable as a PNG of size 512x512.
- Single-channel (grayscale) with bit-depth >= 8 (16-bit preferred).
- Nonzero-pixel ratio (button footprint) in [0.30, 0.85].
- Foreground brightness std >= 10\255 (non-degenerate).
- Pearson correlation between the PNG values and the synthetic z-heightfield >= 0.9.
